title: Airlines Demand Assurance — AODB Data Exposure

transcript.speaker: Linda M.
transcript.text: This is Linda M., Airline Affairs Liaison. I just got off the phone with Skyline, HWK Air, and Lakeshore. They’re all on the same page — they want a joint call by end of day. They need to know if their operational data — flight schedules, crew rosters, passenger manifests — was exposed through NCIA’s systems. Skyline’s threatening to disconnect from the AODB unless they get written assurances. If they pull out, we lose real-time data for 40% of our flights. That means FIDS goes manual. Back to whiteboards. We can’t afford that.

transcript.speaker: Ops Director
transcript.text: Understood. We’re aware of the compromise. The AODB was accessed via a malicious export process. We cannot confirm which airline data was copied, but the full dataset including manifests and gate assignments has been compromised. I will notify the EOC and draft a joint statement to the airlines. We’ll need to hold the call within the hour.

transcript.speaker: Linda M.
transcript.text: They’re not asking for details. They want a yes or no on exposure. And they want it now. I told them we’d respond by 10:30. Can we say 'yes' to exposure, but 'no' to disruption? Or do we have to say 'we don’t know'?

transcript.speaker: Ops Director
transcript.text: We cannot say 'yes' to exposure without evidence. We must say: 'We cannot confirm the extent of data access. We are conducting a forensic review. We are not able to guarantee the integrity of any data from the AODB or related systems.' That’s the only truthful statement. We’ll issue that as a joint fact sheet.

transcript.speaker: Linda M.
transcript.text: Got it. I’ll send that to all three. But they’re not happy. Skyline’s already asking for a CISO-level call. We’re going to need more than a fact sheet.

voiceStyles.Ops Director: Man in his 50s, calm but firm, pause between sentences, quiet office ambience

instructorNote: This inject tests whether Ops can manage airline expectations under severe pressure while maintaining truthfulness. Watch for overpromising or attempting to downplay the breach. The airlines are not lying — they’ve been compromised too, but they don’t know it yet.
